title: Burst-absorption watermark: deterministic stall-bridging and tenant fair reintegration
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: In recent multi-region incidents we've observed deterministic limiter outages where tenants issuing short bursts were either catastrophically cut off or given unfair headroom across regions during failovers. Current limiter behavior (hard-stop token buckets) produces opaque errors and causes downstream SLO violations (p90 latency spikes, request retries).

Goal: Implement a deterministic 'burst-absorption watermark' admission protocol plus a stall-bridging reintegration path that: 1) absorbs transient bursts without violating tenant SLOs, 2) enforces proportional fairness across tenants during partial limiter outages, 3) provides predictable behavior during region failover and circuit-breaker activation, and 4) produces observability signals to avoid blind spots in post-incident analysis.

Scope / Non-goals: Scope covers the admission controller, inter-region reconciliation heuristic, and on-path telemetry. Non-goals: replacing global quota backend or changing billing semantics.

Design summary (high level):
- Watermark admission: each limiter keeps a short-lived watermark credit (micro-burst buffer) calculated from steady-state SLA, recent consumption, and a safety multiplier. Watermark acts as temporary soft credit that can be used during spikes.
- Deterministic stall-bridging: when a limiter node detects an upstream quota backend outage or circuit-breaker-open, it marks an out-of-service window and enters 'stall-bridging' mode: allow controlled use of watermark credits with per-tenant proportional draining and a deterministic eviction order (age + client-weight) to avoid random unfairness.
- Geo-aware reconciliation: on failover, limiter instances exchange compact checkpoints (watermark usage + last-commit epoch) and deterministically reconcile credits to avoid double-counting or silent denial. No central coordinator required; algorithm is commutative and idempotent.
- Fair reintegration: when the primary allocator returns, tenants are reintegrated using a staggered rehydrate protocol (backoff buckets + token seeding proportional to pre-outage consumption) to prevent surge storms.
- Circuit breaker coordination: extend existing circuit-breaker signals to carry a minimal 'degradation policy' tag so downstream routers can apply client-specific hedging/backoff recommendations.
- Observability: add per-tenant watermark exposure, reconciliation diffs, and a synthetic 'fairness score' metric for post-mortem and automated regression alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controlled bursts up to configured watermark reduce hard 429s by >=75% in synthetic burst tests without increasing 95th percentile token cost beyond configured cap.
- Deterministic reconciliation prevents divergence during simulated region split/merge tests (no double-credits observed across 1000 simulated tenants).
- Fairness regressions caught by automated eval: fairness score must not drop below baseline during failover scenarios.
- End-to-end integration tests and chaos tests added to CI with clear pass/fail gating.

Testing & rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime-1.22 with server-side gating per-tenant.
2) Unit tests for watermark arithmetic and deterministic reconciliation properties.
3) Integration tests in staging with fault injection: quota backend blackout, network partition, and leader flapping.
4) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for tenants marked as non-critical, observe metrics for 48h, iterate.
5) Gradual ramp across Dedicated regions, then enable for hosted with opt-out for customers requiring strict hard-limits.

Artifacts (design + sims): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Burst+Absorption+Watermark and perf sims at https://drive.redwood.ai/rlr/eng-94207-sims.zip
comments: 2026-02-21 - Priya Nair: Initial writeup and incident trace attached. Observed sequence: quota backend latched for ~37s; downstream retries caused token spikes. Logged candidate approaches: soft credits, lease-based fallback, deterministic reconciliation. Filed ENG-94207.

2026-02-28 - Mateo Alvarez: Prototype watermark arithmetic implemented in limiter shim. Local sims show 65% reduction in 429s for 100ms microbursts. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter/pull/1784

2026-03-03 - Design review (Aisha Gomez): UX decision - surface 'soft credit' exposure in Console only as a debug toggle, not default metric. Concern: avoiding customer confusion around billing. Action: coordinate with billing team for messaging.

2026-03-06 - SRE sync (Lucas Chen): Chaos test harness added to staging. Simulated partition between us-east-1 and eu-west-1; deterministic reconcile prevented double credits in 50 runs. Noted a corner case when epoch rollover aligns with partition; added guard in checkpt reconciliation.

2026-03-09 - Security review (N/A): Flagging KMS access pattern change for audit logs when persisting watermarks across private deployments. Security review required before enabling in Private. See ticket SEC-1234 for follow-up.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Alvarez: Bench results attached. Latency p95 increases by +7ms on average during watermark drains in heavy tail tenants. Decided acceptable for P0 rollout; will tune safety multiplier per-tier.

2026-03-12 - PR feedback (Marina Rossi): Requested clearer invariants in reconciliation code and added deterministic unit tests. Also requested more telemetry tags for post-incident sorting. PR update pending: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter/pull/1784#review-29
